newsitem.title: UK: Brazil says 95/96 coffee output at 25-26 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says 95/96 coffee output at 25-26 mln bags.

text.p: Brazil's coffee output is estimated at 25-26 million 60-kg bags in 1995/96 (Oct/Sept) and slightly higher demand could mean a domestic deficit that would be met by national stocks, the country's senior coffee official said.
Mauricio Assis, the head of the Industry and Commerce Ministry's primary commodities department, told reporters in London that exports reached 660,000 bags for the first two weeks of October.
Assis, on a visit to London, put 1995/96 exports at 15 million bags and internal consumption at 10 million. A further 2.5 million would be for soluble coffee of which 80 percent are to be exported.
"So there will be a small deficit which will be met by stocks both in private and government hands," he said.
Assis said there are about 13.7 million bags of stocks in government hands, down from 17 million two or three years ago.
"These stocks are used for internal consumption, not for exports," he said.
Of the total 1995/96 production, about 12.4 million bags were from the top growing state of Minas Gerais, and 3.3 million from Sao Paulo, Assis said.
He also said the government had no immediate plan to increase the amount of coffee to be sold at monthly auctions.
"At the moment, the crop is entering the market. We may enhance sales in the future depending on the situation."
He also said Brazil was satisfied with the progress of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries' (ACPC) export programme.
He said overall, the export quotas were being observed by member states and the scheme has helped stabilise prices.
"We don't expect any changes (to the export quotas) in the future," he said.
Assis also said the government was proposing measures to improve domestic coffee consumption.
The plan calls for the increase in local use by 50 percent to 15 million bags by the year 2000.

He also said the government was formulating a policy aimed at enhancing its capacity to provide the market with a more accurate crop forecast. He did not elaborate. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
